raw_response:
I’m already thinking about cash first. Twenty mu is not much, and with some people working outside, the field work still has to fit around who is home. I’ve done this all my life, so I won’t make big changes. Wheat and maize go together on most of my land because that is the steady way here. Cotton gives cash if the price is all right, but it takes more watching and more hand work, so I won’t put too much land into it at my age.

For the wheat-maize land, I’ll keep about 14 mu in that rotation. Wheat is my base crop, and maize follows right after harvest, same as always. I’ll put the better land into wheat and maize because that land responds better to water and fertilizer. I won’t push fertilizer too hard because it costs money, but I also don’t dare use too little and watch the crop turn weak. For cotton, I’ll keep about 6 mu. Cotton can still bring in some money, but it needs more labor for picking and pest watching, so I keep it to an area my family can still handle. I have well water, so if it turns dry, I can save the crop with a few irrigations, but pumping costs money, so I only water at the key times.
